synopsis: Risk-off tone to start a loaded week: US equity-index futures are lower with the Nasdaq (-0.6%) underperforming as a chip-sector rout — aggravated by Alibaba's $10.2bn share placement to fund AI capex, a reminder of how much capital the buildout is soaking up — dents the AI trade ahead of Nvidia earnings.
commentary:
Risk-off tone to start a loaded week: US equity-index futures are lower with the Nasdaq (-0.6%) underperforming as a chip-sector rout — aggravated by Alibaba's $10.2bn share placement to fund AI capex, a reminder of how much capital the buildout is soaking up — dents the AI trade ahead of Nvidia earnings. The bigger macro event is Jackson Hole, where new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh makes his debut and Treasury Secretary Bessent also speaks, with the bond market anxious for direction after weeks of term-premium angst. Treasuries caught a bid overnight, led by the long end (Ultra +0.4%), while the dollar firmed broadly and CAD lagged (-0.6%) after US-Canada trade talks reportedly broke down.

Energy is the puzzle of the morning: crude fell hard — WTI -1.9%, Brent -1.4%, products off 2%+ — even as Bessent teased an "economic D-Day" sanctions announcement on Iran and Tehran threatened 46 vessels in a Strait of Hormuz crackdown. The market seems to be discounting the headlines until it sees how sanctions would actually bite China, the top buyer of Iranian barrels. Nat gas went the other way, Henry Hub +1% and TTF +2.5%, on record-breaking August heat and softer US output. In ags, tariff friction is the driver — arabica hit records on the US-Colombia spat (+1.7%), while corn (+2.7%) and wheat (+1.9%) rallied and sugar and cocoa sold off.

Gold held a modest bid (+0.5%) as a hedge into the week's event risk. Watch Warsh's speech, July core PCE, and any concrete Iran sanctions detail — each can reprice the curve, the dollar and crude in one move.
